Unrequested printed coral ECG trace; the prompt said no printed trace. It is a full QRS line under and beside the strand: peak at about (889,629) above the apex bead, Q dip at about (829,1353), S wave down to about (990,1567), T hump at about (1104,1081). Grid realism. Bold cells hold 4 sub-squares across and 4 or 5 down, so they are mostly rectangles; real ECG paper is a regular 5×5 grid of 1mm squares. Not visible at phone size, but it shows in a zoom.

Small artifacts. A tiny stray wire nub pokes up from the apex bead at x≈893, y 727-748 (about 1.3mm). A hard-edged trapezoid reflection on the heart's lower lobe (x≈1577-1631, y≈1300-1335) reads slightly like a dent at phone size.

No text or logos. Pale pink paper with a coral grid is on palette. Soft top light with crisp specular highlights and real contact shadows; the top third is clean grid for a headline. It is the strongest idea in the set and reads in one second. Why 8.0: the second printed trace, the gunmetal-dark beads against the brighter paper, and the slightly small piece keep it below run-as-is.
fix: Do not run as-is. Fastest route is retouch: remove the printed coral trace (rebuild the grid lines under it), delete the apex wire nub, and soften the trapezoid reflection on the heart. For a reshoot, keep the prompt and add 'the paper is blank ECG grid with no printed trace at all; the bracelet is the only line; every bold 5mm square holds exactly 5×5 small 1mm squares'. Make the strand about 20% larger against the grid: each bead covers 6 small squares, and the heart is 2.5-3 bold squares wide. Add a pale overhead reflector so the beads mirror the pink paper and read bright silver, not gunmetal.

reasons: Construction is garbled and the piece reads as a double-strand bracelet (rules 1 and 2). The beads run as two parallel strands. At top-left, two loose ends each finish in a small silver bead with a bare, open eye-pin wire hook (about (355,517) and (465,499)); neither has a clasp part. The T-bar hangs from a jump ring inside the ring instead of terminating the opposite end.
Part count is wrong as a result: 4 strand ends and 4 small end beads, where the real piece is one strand with 2 ends, 2 small end beads, and the T-bar and ring on opposite ends.
Garbled detail: crumpled, melted silver spacer bits sit at several bead junctions (for example about (418,1157) and (536,1230)) instead of fine silver links.

notes: 25 large beads in total: 6 + 6 in the two vertical columns and 13 in the doubled horizontal run. The count is within tolerance, but split across two strands.

What is right: one smooth, puffed, polished gold heart on a jump ring from the ring, and a straight T-bar. The beads are bright mirror silver (median L about 140), the closest to the brief's 'bright' silver in this set.

The concept is not delivered. There is no single melodic line along one stave and no gold note set a little apart at the end; the strand is a doubled L-shape crossing several staves, and the T-bar lies across the ring.

The staves are blank (no clefs, notes or numbers), so there is no text. The paper reads aged cream-beige (about 240,225,210, hue about 27°), on the warm-beige edge of the palette. The prop is a whole dried rose head, not a petal, at lower left.
fix: Regenerate. State 'ONE single strand with exactly two ends: the straight gold T-bar on one end and the gold ring with the heart on the other; no loose wire ends; fine silver links between beads'. Lay it in one gentle wave along a single stave, with the ring and heart set a little apart at the end. State the scale: 'each 6mm bead covers about three quarters of one stave's height; the heart is about two staves tall'. Use listing-4 as the strand reference, and ivory or blush-tinted manuscript paper instead of aged cream.

fix: Do not run as-is. Reshoot and keep the low warm side light and long shadows. Ask for 'pale ivory goatskin, clean, with only faint natural mottling, no brown stains' and a lighter blush wall. Move closer so the loop fills about 40% of the frame width. Use a pale reflector so the beads read bright mirror silver. Add 'the T-bar's centre loop passes through the ring; the toggle is fastened'.

No text and no other jewellery. Blush silk is on palette. The macro depth of field works: the bracelet is sharp and the palm softly blurred.

Why 8.0. The idea reads at once, and the heart is the brightest, sharpest thing. But the soft palm and cropped fingers fill the top third where the brief wanted calm silk for the headline (copy space is left only at top right), and the dark beads weaken the silver/gold contrast.
fix: Close to runnable. In a reshoot, keep the palm-up wrist, the heart on the inner wrist, the macro optics, the scale and the silk. Move the hand down or out so the top third is calm blush silk: 'fingers curled gently out of frame at the left; the top third is empty silk'. Add a pale reflector or window reflection so the beads mirror bright light and read bright silver. Nudge the heart toward the thumb side, onto the pulse.
